title: 06. Memory, State & HITL: LangGraph: Memory
summary: This notebook covers the two kinds of memory in LangGraph with examples for each:

sections.title: Short-Term Memory | Long-Term Memory
sections.body:
This notebook covers the **two kinds of memory** in LangGraph with
examples for each:

| Kind | Lives in | Scope | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Short-term** | `checkpointer` (e.g. `MemorySaver`) | one `thread_id` | running chat, counter |
| **Long-term**  | `store` (e.g. `InMemoryStore`)      | across threads / users | user profile, preferences |

### Short-term memory
The **state** of a graph is saved by a **checkpointer** after every node.
Two `invoke` calls that use the same `thread_id` will share state — the
second call sees what the first one wrote.  This is how a chatbot
"remembers" the current conversation.

### Long-term memory
A **store** is a separate key-value layer that lives **outside** the
thread.  You write to it from inside a node (`store.put(namespace, key, value)`)
and read from it from any other thread or even a different graph
(`store.get(namespace, key)`).  This is how an app remembers facts
about a user **between** conversations.

```
+-------------------+        +-------------------+
|   thread A        |        |   thread B        |
|  (checkpointer)   |        |  (checkpointer)   |
|   short-term      |        |   short-term      |
+---------+---------+        +---------+---------+
          \                            /
           \                          /
            v                        v
          +----------------------------+
          |          STORE             |    <-- long-term, shared
          |  ("user:42", "profile")    |
          +----------------------------+
```

```python
# ============================================================
# SETUP - Run this cell first!
# ============================================================
from langchain_groq import ChatGroq
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, START, END
from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import MemorySaver
from langgraph.store.memory import InMemoryStore
from langgraph.store.base import BaseStore
from typing import TypedDict, List, Annotated
from operator import add
from IPython.display import Image, display

api_key = "YOUR_GROQ_API_KEY"   # <-- replace with your key
llm = ChatGroq(api_key=api_key, model="openai/gpt-oss-20b")

print("Setup complete! LLM ready.")
```

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
Short-term memory = state automatically persisted **per `thread_id`** by
a **checkpointer**.

The pattern is always:

```python
app = graph.compile(checkpointer=MemorySaver())
cfg = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "abc"}}

app.invoke({...}, config=cfg)   # writes state
app.invoke({...}, config=cfg)   # sees the previous state
```

sections.title: Example 1 (Easy): Counter Across Invokes
sections.body:
**What it does:** Each call to `invoke` increments a counter that lives
in the checkpointed state.  Two different `thread_id`s have two
independent counters.

```python
class CountState(TypedDict):
    count: int

def bump(state: CountState):
    return {"count": state.get("count", 0) + 1}

g = StateGraph(CountState)
g.add_node("bump", bump)
g.add_edge(START, "bump")
g.add_edge("bump", END)

app_count = g.compile(checkpointer=MemorySaver())

cfg_a = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "user-A"}}
cfg_b = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "user-B"}}

for _ in range(3):
    app_count.invoke({}, config=cfg_a)
app_count.invoke({}, config=cfg_b)

print("user-A count:", app_count.get_state(cfg_a).values["count"])  # 3
print("user-B count:", app_count.get_state(cfg_b).values["count"])  # 1
```

sections.title: Example 2 (Medium): Chat History Within a Thread
sections.body:
**What it does:** Each `invoke` appends the new user message *and* the
LLM reply to a running list.  Because state is persisted per
`thread_id`, the LLM can answer follow-up questions like "what's my
name?" using earlier turns in the same thread.

**Key idea:** the `Annotated[list, add]` reducer **accumulates** values
on each update instead of overwriting them.

```python
class ChatState(TypedDict):
    messages: Annotated[List[dict], add]   # accumulated

def chat_node(state: ChatState):
    # Build a single prompt from the running history
    history = "\n".join(f"{m['role']}: {m['content']}" for m in state["messages"])
    reply = llm.invoke(history).content
    return {"messages": [{"role": "assistant", "content": reply}]}

g = StateGraph(ChatState)
g.add_node("chat", chat_node)
g.add_edge(START, "chat")
g.add_edge("chat", END)
app_chat = g.compile(checkpointer=MemorySaver())

cfg = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "chat-1"}}

# Turn 1
r1 = app_chat.invoke(
    {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hi, my name is Praveer."}]}, config=cfg)
print("A1:", r1["messages"][-1]["content"])

# Turn 2 - the model should still know the name
r2 = app_chat.invoke(
    {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is my name?"}]}, config=cfg)
print("A2:", r2["messages"][-1]["content"])
```

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
Long-term memory = a **store** that survives across threads.

Inside a node, declare a `store: BaseStore` parameter — LangGraph injects
the store that you passed to `compile(store=...)`.

The API is:

```python
store.put(namespace_tuple, key, value_dict)
item = store.get(namespace_tuple, key)   # item.value is the dict (or None)
items = store.search(namespace_tuple)    # list everything in the namespace
```

A **namespace** is a tuple like `("user", "42")` that groups related keys.

sections.title: Example 3 (Easy): User Profile Across Threads
sections.body:
**What it does:** Thread A saves a user's favourite colour in the store.
Thread B (a different `thread_id`) reads it back.  The checkpointer
*cannot* do this — only the store can.

```python
class ProfileState(TypedDict):
    user_id: str
    action: str         # "save" or "load"
    colour: str
    loaded: str

def profile_node(state: ProfileState, *, store: BaseStore):
    ns = ("user", state["user_id"])
    if state["action"] == "save":
        store.put(ns, "profile", {"favourite_colour": state["colour"]})
        return {"loaded": ""}
    item = store.get(ns, "profile")
    return {"loaded": (item.value["favourite_colour"] if item else "<unknown>")}

g = StateGraph(ProfileState)
g.add_node("profile", profile_node)
g.add_edge(START, "profile")
g.add_edge("profile", END)

store = InMemoryStore()
app_prof = g.compile(checkpointer=MemorySaver(), store=store)

# Thread A writes
app_prof.invoke(
    {"user_id": "42", "action": "save", "colour": "green", "loaded": ""},
    config={"configurable": {"thread_id": "t-A"}},
)

# Thread B reads (different thread_id, same user)
r = app_prof.invoke(
    {"user_id": "42", "action": "load", "colour": "", "loaded": ""},
    config={"configurable": {"thread_id": "t-B"}},
)
print("Loaded in a new thread:", r["loaded"])   # 'green'
```

sections.title: Example 4 (Medium): Accumulating Notes per User
sections.body:
**What it does:** Each call adds a note to a user's notebook.  Notes are
stored as separate keys under the same namespace, so we can list them all
later with `store.search`.

**Key idea:** the store is a **key-value** layer — you decide the key
scheme (here, an incrementing `note-N`).

```python
class NoteState(TypedDict):
    user_id: str
    new_note: str
    all_notes: List[str]

def add_note(state: NoteState, *, store: BaseStore):
    ns = ("user", state["user_id"], "notes")
    existing = store.search(ns)
    next_id = f"note-{len(existing) + 1}"
    store.put(ns, next_id, {"text": state["new_note"]})
    refreshed = store.search(ns)
    return {"all_notes": [it.value["text"] for it in refreshed]}

g = StateGraph(NoteState)
g.add_node("add_note", add_note)
g.add_edge(START, "add_note")
g.add_edge("add_note", END)

store = InMemoryStore()
app_notes = g.compile(checkpointer=MemorySaver(), store=store)

for note in ["Buy milk", "Read LangGraph docs", "Call mom"]:
    r = app_notes.invoke(
        {"user_id": "42", "new_note": note, "all_notes": []},
        config={"configurable": {"thread_id": f"add-{note}"}},
    )
print("All notes for user 42:", r["all_notes"])
```

sections.title: Example 5 (LLM): Chatbot With Both Memories
sections.body:
**What it does:** A single graph uses

* **short-term memory** (checkpointer) to remember the **current
  conversation** within a thread, and
* **long-term memory** (store) to remember **facts about the user**
  across conversations.

Each turn we (1) load the user's known facts from the store, (2) ask the
LLM to reply using both the facts and the running chat history, and
(3) extract any new fact the user just told us and write it back to the
store.

```
START --> [load_facts] --> [chat (LLM)] --> [save_facts] --> END
             (store)        (checkpointer)     (store)
```

```python
class BotState(TypedDict):
    user_id: str
    messages: Annotated[List[dict], add]
    facts: List[str]

def load_facts(state: BotState, *, store: BaseStore):
    ns = ("user", state["user_id"], "facts")
    items = store.search(ns)
    return {"facts": [it.value["text"] for it in items]}

def chat(state: BotState):
    fact_block = "\n".join(f"- {f}" for f in state["facts"]) or "(none yet)"
    history = "\n".join(f"{m['role']}: {m['content']}" for m in state["messages"])
    prompt = (
        "You are a helpful assistant.\n"
        f"Known facts about the user:\n{fact_block}\n\n"
        f"Conversation so far:\n{history}\n\n"
        "Reply to the last user message."
    )
    reply = llm.invoke(prompt).content
    return {"messages": [{"role": "assistant", "content": reply}]}

def save_facts(state: BotState, *, store: BaseStore):
    # Ask the LLM to pull out any new factual statement from the latest user msg
    last_user = next((m["content"] for m in reversed(state["messages"])
                      if m["role"] == "user"), "")
    extract = llm.invoke(
        "Extract ONE short factual statement about the user from this message, "
        "or reply with the single word NONE.\n\nMessage: " + last_user
    ).content.strip()
    if extract and extract.upper() != "NONE":
        ns = ("user", state["user_id"], "facts")
        store.put(ns, f"fact-{len(store.search(ns)) + 1}", {"text": extract})
    return {}

g = StateGraph(BotState)
g.add_node("load_facts", load_facts)
g.add_node("chat", chat)
g.add_node("save_facts", save_facts)
g.add_edge(START, "load_facts")
g.add_edge("load_facts", "chat")
g.add_edge("chat", "save_facts")
g.add_edge("save_facts", END)

store = InMemoryStore()
app_bot = g.compile(checkpointer=MemorySaver(), store=store)
display(Image(app_bot.get_graph().draw_mermaid_png()))
```

```python
# Conversation 1
cfg1 = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "conv-1"}}
r = app_bot.invoke(
    {"user_id": "42",
     "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hi! I love hiking in the Alps."}],
     "facts": []},
    config=cfg1,
)
print("Bot:", r["messages"][-1]["content"])

# Brand new conversation (different thread) - facts should still be known
cfg2 = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "conv-2"}}
r = app_bot.invoke(
    {"user_id": "42",
     "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Suggest a weekend activity for me."}],
     "facts": []},
    config=cfg2,
)
print("Bot (new thread):", r["messages"][-1]["content"])
```

sections.title: Recap
sections.body:
| Need | Use |
|---|---|
| Persist state inside one conversation / `thread_id` | **Checkpointer** (short-term) |
| Persist facts / preferences across conversations or users | **Store** (long-term) |
| Both at the same time (typical chatbot) | Compile with **`checkpointer=` and `store=`** |

Key APIs:

* `graph.compile(checkpointer=MemorySaver(), store=InMemoryStore())`
* Inside a node: declare `store: BaseStore` to receive the store
* `store.put(ns, key, value_dict)` / `store.get(ns, key)` / `store.search(ns)`
* `app.get_state(config)` to inspect the short-term state of a thread.
